description: Records what the user says ACTUALLY happened in a gym session (reps, weights, RPE, notes), because the watch only records the guide's planned text. Writes only the local file ~/.suunto-mcp/journal.json (SUUNTO_JOURNAL_PATH overrides it) and never contacts Suunto. One entry per workoutKey: logging the same workoutKey again REPLACES that entry, and the result returns the previous one as `replaced` so nothing is lost silently. A call with no note, no feeling, no tags and no exercises is refused ('nothing to log'): it would wipe the stored entry. Unknown fields at any level (e.g. `weight`) are refused with an error naming the field, never dropped: use `kg` inside a set. get_exercise_history attaches the entry as `journal` and uses the top set's kg as the load when sets carry kg. Only record what the user told you; leave out what they did not say. Exercise names should be the ones get_exercise_history or compare_workout_to_plan show. Limits: reps integer 0-200, kg 0-1000, rpe 1-10, texts up to 500 characters, at most 40 exercises and 20 sets each, at most 8 tags of 1-24 characters each (trimmed; no control characters; no duplicates, ignoring case; stored on the entry; get_tag_effects compares the nights after tagged sessions with the others, get_exercise_history does not use them). A call with ONLY tags does not replace the entry: it sets the entry's tags and keeps its note, feeling and exercises (a tags-only entry is created when none exists). Optional `source: 'draft'` marks an entry made from a confirmed draft_session_log. Output: { saved, replaced, entries }.

exercises.description: Per exercise what was actually done. Leave out exercises that went as planned.

name.description: Exercise name as in get_exercise_history, e.g. 'Back Squat'.

note.description: A note on this exercise, e.g. 'left knee felt tight'.

sets.description: The sets in order, as done.

note.description: How the session went overall, in the user's words, e.g. 'all as planned except squat set 3'.

source.description: Pass 'draft' when the exercises come from a draft_session_log that the user confirmed or corrected (the reps and weights began as the guide's plan). Stored on the entry; nothing else changes.

tags.description: Optional short labels for the session, e.g. ['deload', 'poor-sleep'] (at most 8, each 1-24 characters, trimmed, no duplicates). Sent alone, they set the tags of the existing entry without touching the rest.

workoutKey.description: The 24-character workoutKey of the session, from list_workouts or get_daily_snapshot.

name: log_session
title: Log what actually happened in a session
